messages.author: 5e649bb0b1e892e9
messages.subject: Problem with GLAD for Xba arrays
parts:
Dear Henrik

I have just run GLAD for Sty arrays in one xterm and for Xba arrays in
another xterm using the same code.

Here is the relevant output for Mapping250K_Sty:
Loading required package: GLAD
Loading required package: aws
Loading required package: tcltk
Loading Tcl/Tk interface ... done
[1] "Have fun with GLAD"
Generating ChromosomeExplorer report...
Loading required package: Cairo
Generating ChromosomeExplorer report...done
There were 50 or more warnings (use warnings() to see the first 50)

As you see, everything is ok.


In contrast, here is the output for Mapping50K_Xba240:
Loading required package: GLAD
Loading required package: aws
Loading required package: tcltk
Loading Tcl/Tk interface ... done
[1] "Have fun with GLAD"
Generating ChromosomeExplorer report...
Loading required package: Cairo
Error in matrix(NA, nrow = max(uUnitSizes), ncol =
length(unitNames)) :
invalid 'nrow' value (too large or NA)
In addition: There were 50 or more warnings (use warnings() to see the
first 50)
Generating ChromosomeExplorer report...done


Running the code manually for Mapping50K_Xba240 I get:
> cesList <- effectSet(aroma.xba)
> model <- GladModel(cesList, NULL)
> arrays <- indexOfArrays(model)
> ce <- ChromosomeExplorer(model);
> tmp <- process(ce, arrays=arrays, chromosomes=NULL, force=F, verbose=T);
Generating ChromosomeExplorer report...
Error in matrix(NA, nrow = max(uUnitSizes), ncol =
length(unitNames)) :
invalid 'nrow' value (too large or NA)
Generating ChromosomeExplorer report...done
> tmp <- process(ce, arrays=3, chromosomes=NULL, force=F, verbose=T);
Generating ChromosomeExplorer report...
Error in matrix(NA, nrow = max(uUnitSizes), ncol =
length(unitNames)) :
invalid 'nrow' value (too large or NA)
Generating ChromosomeExplorer report...done


However, when I do:
> tmp <- process(ce, arrays=3, chromosomes=1:23, force=F, verbose=T)
Generating ChromosomeExplorer report...done

Now, everything is ok. Thus it seems that setting "chromosomes=NULL"
seems to call: chromsosome=24.
Could this be the reason for the error message?

Here is the:
> sessionInfo()

x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu

locale:

Yes, it could/is likely to be related. Try:

ces <- getListOfChipEffectSets(model)[[1]];
cdf <- getCdf(ces);
gi <- getGenomeInformation(cdf);
print(range(getChromosomes(gi)));
## [1] 1 24
print(gi)
UgpGenomeInformation:
Name: Mapping50K_Xba240
Tags: na24,HB20080214
Pathname: C:/Documents and Settings/hb/My Documents/My Data/annotationData/chipT
ypes/Mapping50K_Xba240/Mapping50K_Xba240,na24,HB20080214.ugp
File size: 288.61kB
RAM: 2.48MB
Chip type: Mapping50K_Xba240

units <- getUnitsOnChromosome(gi, 24);
print(units);
[1] 10110

So, there is indeed one single Chr24 locus in Mapping50K_Xba240.
Since this is a single value, it might be that it extracts a single
row/column in a matrix/data frame and then the dimension is dropped,
that is, the bug is then a missing drop=FALSE.

Please let me know the traceback() so I can track where/when it occurs.

/Henrik

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: Problem with GLAD for Xba arrays
parts:
Hi,

I've managed to reproduce this problem and it occurs because in the
latest annotation data files (UGP generated from the Affymetrix
NetAffx CSV file) there is a single unit on Chr24. There were a few
function in aroma.affymetrix that dropped the dimensions of
matrices/data.frames in this case causing the error. I've committed
patches for this. Do:

library(aroma.affymetrix);
downloadPackagePatch("aroma.affymetrix");

and retry. Let us know if it works.

/Henrik
